issue.title: Record the capture inbox routing ownership and atomic-batch decision
issue.description: Proposed by bob-cli-bk.1 note #1, bob-cli-bk.2 note #1, bob-cli-bk.3 note #1, and bob-cli-bk.4 note #1. Source: plan:202610/capture_inbox_routing.md; bob-cli commits bb52dd0a/4f13e979 and bob-mac-capture 2968311/7bfa312. All-status memory search and one-week sweep found no duplicate. bob-cli-4t concerns Obsidian gesture routing with close exclusions and different atomicity; it is related, not the same decision. No active unrelated epic owns this intentionally deferred capture decision record. Small: one evidence-backed strand, no behavior work.

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Add decisions/capture-asks-where-inbox-tasks-go.md in the decisions web, using the approved capture inbox routing plan and the phase commits as evidence: bob detects changed existing inbox tasks, supplies destinations, and applies action then move in one capture batch; Mac only asks and submits opaque answers. Record rejected separate capture/move calls, draft-marker answers, move-first ordering, and capture-targets discovery; include extra snapshot-scan cost and the condition for reopening. Link decisions:mac-capture-is-a-thin-client and decisions:unblocked-tasks-are-offered. Obtain memory authorization and regenerate with sase memory init. This records the existing accepted behavior and does not change it.

issue.creation_reason: Epic bob-cli-bk automatically declined its unrequested memory_decision_record decision without human review; all four phases recorded the required proposal for landing triage. Preserve one scoped proposal for later approval.

payload.description: Related inbox routing design records; 4t owns Obsidian gesture behavior, br owns capture atomic batch and thin-client ownership
